sub_graphs.title: EIP-4: EIP Classification Framework
sub_graphs.description: Models how EIPs are classified into protocol layers, affecting which stakeholder groups must review and implement changes

nodes.label: EIP Submitted for Classification
nodes.description: A new EIP has been submitted and requires layer classification

nodes.label: Classify EIP by Layer
nodes.description: Determine which protocol layer the EIP affects: Consensus, Networking, API/RPC, or Applications

nodes.label: EIP Classified as Consensus Layer
nodes.description: EIP affects cryptographic commitments and settlement; changes can cause network partitioning

nodes.label: EIP Classified as Networking Layer
nodes.description: EIP affects devp2p wire protocols and peer-to-peer communication

nodes.label: EIP Classified as API/RPC Layer
nodes.description: EIP affects application-accessible RPC calls and interfaces

nodes.label: EIP Classified as Applications Layer
nodes.description: EIP affects high-level standards and abstractions built on Ethereum

external_entities.name: EIP Author
external_entities.description: External party proposing an Ethereum Improvement Proposal

sub_graphs.title: EIP-4: Consensus Layer Change Impact
sub_graphs.description: Models the potential network impact when consensus layer EIPs are implemented inconsistently

nodes.label: Consensus Layer Change Proposed
nodes.description: A change to consensus rules has been proposed via an EIP

nodes.label: Evaluate Network Partition Risk
nodes.description: Assess whether disagreements on consensus layer changes could cause network partitioning

nodes.label: Network Remains Unified
nodes.description: All nodes agree on consensus rules; network operates normally

nodes.label: Network Partitioned
nodes.description: Disagreement on consensus rules causes network to split into incompatible chains

external_entities.name: Core Developers
external_entities.description: Ethereum client developers responsible for implementing consensus changes

ambiguities.text: The boundaries between layers are not precisely defined, particularly for EIPs that span multiple layers.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume an EIP is classified by its primary impact layer, with secondary layers noted but not affecting primary classification.

ambiguities.text: No explicit process is defined for handling EIPs that affect multiple layers simultaneously.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume multi-layer EIPs require review from all affected stakeholder groups.

implicit_assumptions.description: All client implementations will adopt consensus layer changes uniformly.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Network partitioning and chain splits if implementations disagree on consensus rules.

implicit_assumptions.description: EIP authors correctly identify the layer their proposal affects.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect stakeholder review, potentially missing security implications.
